title: Exactly one WakeReport when the human comes back
action: Plan Phase 3, second half (per 9f5cd250 and 66c4c251): on `bee supervisor back`, emit EXACTLY ONE WakeReport for the window sup-8 just closed. Shape is fixed and enforced by a test, not by prose: markdown, AT MOST 10 lines, exactly four sections in this order — 'What happened', 'What was decided', 'What needs you', 'Next action'. Build it in packages/bee-rs/crates/bee/src/verbs/supervisor.rs from records already in the store or already readable in .bee, never from a new subsystem: observation rows in the window (what happened), decision-log events whose timestamp falls in the window (what was decided), queued intervention/escalation rows released by back plus any waiting-on mark (what needs you), and a single next-action line. Order items inside a section by impact-if-wrong DESCENDING (66c4c251): urgent before escalation before intervention, and a one-way-door decision before a reversible one; when nothing distinguishes two rows keep store order. Truncation is part of the shape, not a bug: when the honest content exceeds 10 lines, keep the highest-impact items and end with a '+N more' count on the last line — never silently drop. An empty window still yields a legal report whose sections say plainly that nothing happened. Persist each rendered report as a row in .bee/supervisor/reports.jsonl keyed by the window id, and add `bee supervisor report [--window <id>] [--json]` that READS the stored report and never regenerates it. Exactly-once is the hard rule: a second `back` cannot produce a second report for the same window, and `report` called twice returns the same bytes. Fire exactly ONE notification through the sup-7 notifier seam (notifier_argv/spawn_notifier), best-effort, honoring the same supervisor.notify opt-out, and never let a failed notifier fail `back`. Tests in the same tests module: away, plant three events of different impact, back -> exactly one stored report, at most 10 lines, four sections in order, highest impact first; back twice stores one report; an empty window renders a legal report; over-long content ends in '+N more'; report reads back byte-identical; notify disabled builds no argv. Regen deferred to the wave barrier.

truths: back on a window with events stores exactly one report of at most 10 lines with the four sections in order
a second back stores no second report and report returns the same bytes

prohibitions: no second report for one window
a failed notifier never fails back

trace.outcome: back renders and stores exactly one 4-section WakeReport per window; supervisor report reads it; one best-effort notification through the sup-7 seam
deviations: The report notification is a sibling of notifier_argv (report_notifier_argv) rather than notifier_argv called with a fabricated mailbox row — a WakeReport is not an urgent intervention, so a fake row would have lied to every reader of the store; it shares NOTIFIER, spawn_notifier and the same supervisor.notify opt-out, so no second transport exists — found a better route

Added the flag name --window and bumped catalog.rs PINNED_FLAG_COUNT 194 -> 195 with the reason recorded there: --id already means a mailbox row id on this same supervisor surface, and a stored report is keyed by a row of a different store (the presence window) — the ratchet's own documented process, same reasoning sup-2 recorded for --target-session — something else had to be fixed first

One sup-8 test (away_and_back_write_nothing_outside_the_supervisor_store) now expects reports.jsonl beside interventions.jsonl and presence.jsonl, because back writes the report inside the supervisor store — hit an unforeseen obstacle

One-way-door ranking for decisions reads the irreversible member the decision log actually carries (type supersede, or a non-empty supersedes) because the log has no explicit door field; the fuller confidence x door predicate is Phase 4 (a8f4b8ab) — the plan was wrong about a fact
